---
title: "JQI_JobSatisfaction_PersonalFinance"
output: html_document
---

```{r Step 1, include=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# JQI: Job Satisfaction and Personal Financial Satisfaction
# ============================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(broom)
library(car)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load data
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_gss <- readRDS(
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "gss_job_quality_primary_2000_2024.rds"
  )
)


# ============================================================
# 2. Construct outcomes
# ============================================================

jqi_satfin <- jqi_gss %>%
  mutate(

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Job satisfaction
    # 1 = Very satisfied
    # 2 = Moderately satisfied
    # 3 = A little dissatisfied
    # 4 = Very dissatisfied
    #
    # Reverse so higher = greater satisfaction
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    job_satisfaction = case_when(
      as.numeric(satjob) == 1 ~ 4,
      as.numeric(satjob) == 2 ~ 3,
      as.numeric(satjob) == 3 ~ 2,
      as.numeric(satjob) == 4 ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Personal financial satisfaction
    # 1 = Pretty well satisfied
    # 2 = More or less satisfied
    # 3 = Not satisfied at all
    #
    # Reverse so higher = greater satisfaction
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    financial_satisfaction = case_when(
      as.numeric(satfin) == 1 ~ 3,
      as.numeric(satfin) == 2 ~ 2,
      as.numeric(satfin) == 3 ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )

  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(job_satisfaction),
    !is.na(financial_satisfaction),
    !is.na(compensation),
    !is.na(benefits),
    !is.na(earnings_stability)
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Sample description
# ------------------------------------------------------------

nrow(jqi_satfin)

jqi_satfin %>%
  count(year)

jqi_satfin %>%
  count(industry_common)


# ============================================================
# 3. Basic relationship
# ============================================================

m_satfin_job <- lm(
  financial_satisfaction ~ job_satisfaction,
  data = jqi_satfin
)

print(summary(m_satfin_job))


# ============================================================
# 4. JOB SATISFACTION × COMPENSATION
# ============================================================

m_satfin_job_comp <- lm(
  financial_satisfaction ~
    job_satisfaction * compensation,
  data = jqi_satfin
)

print(summary(m_satfin_job_comp))


# ============================================================
# 5. JOB SATISFACTION × BENEFITS
# ============================================================

m_satfin_job_benefits <- lm(
  financial_satisfaction ~
    job_satisfaction * benefits,
  data = jqi_satfin
)

print(summary(m_satfin_job_benefits))


# ============================================================
# 6. JOB SATISFACTION × EARNINGS STABILITY
# ============================================================

m_satfin_job_earnings <- lm(
  financial_satisfaction ~
    job_satisfaction * earnings_stability,
  data = jqi_satfin
)

print(summary(m_satfin_job_earnings))


# ============================================================
# 7. FULL JOINT MODEL
# ============================================================

m_satfin_job_jqi <- lm(
  financial_satisfaction ~
    job_satisfaction * compensation +
    job_satisfaction * benefits +
    job_satisfaction * earnings_stability,
  data = jqi_satfin
)

print(summary(m_satfin_job_jqi))


# ============================================================
# 8. Joint test of all three interactions
# ============================================================

linearHypothesis(
  m_satfin_job_jqi,
  c(
    "job_satisfaction:compensation = 0",
    "job_satisfaction:benefits = 0",
    "job_satisfaction:earnings_stability = 0"
  )
)


# ============================================================
# 9. Multicollinearity
# ============================================================

vif(m_satfin_job_jqi)


# ============================================================
# 10. Year-specific joint models
# ============================================================

yearly_satfin_job <- jqi_satfin %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  group_modify(~ {

    model <- lm(
      financial_satisfaction ~
        job_satisfaction * compensation +
        job_satisfaction * benefits +
        job_satisfaction * earnings_stability,
      data = .x
    )

    tidy(model) %>%
      filter(
        term %in% c(
          "job_satisfaction",
          "job_satisfaction:compensation",
          "job_satisfaction:benefits",
          "job_satisfaction:earnings_stability"
        )
      )

  }) %>%
  ungroup()

yearly_satfin_job



# ============================================================
# Formal tests of temporal heterogeneity
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Restricted model:
# JQI moderation of the job satisfaction → financial
# satisfaction relationship is constant over time
# ------------------------------------------------------------

m_satfin_job_time_restricted <- lm(
  financial_satisfaction ~
    job_satisfaction * compensation +
    job_satisfaction * benefits +
    job_satisfaction * earnings_stability +

    job_satisfaction * factor(year) +
    compensation * factor(year) +
    benefits * factor(year) +
    earnings_stability * factor(year),

  data = jqi_satfin
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Full model:
# JQI moderation of the job satisfaction → financial
# satisfaction relationship is allowed to vary by year
# ------------------------------------------------------------

m_satfin_job_time_full <- lm(
  financial_satisfaction ~
    job_satisfaction * compensation * factor(year) +
    job_satisfaction * benefits * factor(year) +
    job_satisfaction * earnings_stability * factor(year),

  data = jqi_satfin
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Overall test:
# Does the three-way interaction structure vary by year?
# ------------------------------------------------------------

anova(
  m_satfin_job_time_restricted,
  m_satfin_job_time_full
)


# ============================================================
# Component-specific tests
# ============================================================

# Job satisfaction × compensation × year

comp_three_way_terms <- grep(
  "^job_satisfaction:compensation:factor\\(year\\)",
  names(coef(m_satfin_job_time_full)),
  value = TRUE
)

linearHypothesis(
  m_satfin_job_time_full,
  comp_three_way_terms
)


# Job satisfaction × benefits × year
benefits_three_way_terms <- grep(
  "^job_satisfaction:factor\\(year\\).*:benefits$",
  names(coef(m_satfin_job_time_full)),
  value = TRUE
)

benefits_three_way_terms

linearHypothesis(
  m_satfin_job_time_full,
  benefits_three_way_terms
)

# Job satisfaction × earnings stability × year

earnings_three_way_terms <- grep(
  "^job_satisfaction:factor\\(year\\).*:earnings_stability$",
  names(coef(m_satfin_job_time_full)),
  value = TRUE
)

earnings_three_way_terms

linearHypothesis(
  m_satfin_job_time_full,
  earnings_three_way_terms
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Extract year-specific earnings-stability interactions
# ------------------------------------------------------------

earnings_moderation_year <- yearly_satfin_job %>%
  filter(
    term == "job_satisfaction:earnings_stability"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    conf_low = estimate - 1.96 * std.error,
    conf_high = estimate + 1.96 * std.error
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_earnings_moderation_year <- ggplot(
  earnings_moderation_year,
  aes(x = year, y = estimate)
) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = conf_low, ymax = conf_high),
    width = 0
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(2004, 2024, by = 2),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.08))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Earnings Stability Moderates the Job–Finance Relationship",
    subtitle = "Year-specific interaction between job satisfaction and earnings stability",
    x = "GSS year",
    y = "Job satisfaction × earnings stability coefficient"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

p_earnings_moderation_year

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Save
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ggsave(
  filename = here(
    "04_figures",
    "JobSatisfaction_FinancialSatisfaction_EarningsStability_Year.png"
  ),
  plot = p_earnings_moderation_year,
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)

# ============================================================
# 11. Save results
# ============================================================

write_csv(
  yearly_satfin_job,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "JQI_JobSatisfaction_PersonalFinance_YearSpecific.csv"
  )
)
```
